We’re a technology company shaping the future of networking, guided by innovation, integrity, and collaboration. Through development opportunities, meaningful work, and flexibility, Ciena supports growth and well-being—on and off the job. Connect with a career that matters. 
 Reporting to a Senior Manager, Hardware Engineering, you will work alongside experienced hardware, optical, firmware, reliability, manufacturing, and test engineers responsible for designing, ramping, and sustaining Ciena’s flagship WaveLogic™ optical modems. These products enable data rates of up to 1,600 Gbps and are used by many of the world’s largest telecommunications companies and cloud providers. In this role, you will help improve product yield, support manufacturing ramp, investigate technical issues, and drive hardware, test, or process changes that improve product quality and manufacturability. 
 This role provides a unique opportunity to develop a deep understanding of WaveLogic optical modems, from product design through manufacturing ramp and volume production. You will gain insight into the processes required to build a high-performance, high-volume product, while making contributions that directly support Ciena’s ability to deliver to customers and grow this flagship product line. 
 How You Will Contribute:  
 In this intermediate engineering role, you will support product ramp and sustaining activities, with a focus on yield improvement through test, design, and process improvements. You will combine manufacturing data analysis with hands-on lab debug and cross-functional execution to identify issues, recommend corrective actions, and help drive them to closure. 
 Hands-on lab debug: Perform hardware and optical debug of failed modules to identify root cause, validate hypotheses, and define corrective actions using lab measurements and engineering analysis. 
 Yield data analysis: Review large-scale manufacturing and test data to assess design, process, or test changes that improve factory yield.  Analyze trends, outliers, and common failure modes, then work with cross-functional teams to define practical corrective actions. 
 Change management: Plan, coordinate, validate, and release design, test, or process change orders that support yield improvement, ramp readiness, product quality, and manufacturability. 
 Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with hardware, optical, firmware, test, reliability, manufacturing, operations, and supplier-facing teams to drive technical issues to closure. 
 Documentation and communication: Summarize data analysis, debug findings, recommendations, validation results, and change plans clearly for technical and program stakeholders. 
 The Must Haves:  
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, Engineering Physics, or equivalent. 
 2–5 years of experience in hardware engineering, electrical engineering, optical hardware, telecommunications equipment, networking platforms, manufacturing test, or another complex electronic-product environment. 
 Familiarity with product lifecycle stages, including development, qualification, ramp, volume manufacturing, sustaining, field support, or end-of-life. 
 Demonstrated proficiency with statistical analysis techniques such as histogram distributions, Q-Q plots, standard deviation, process capability, Cp, Cpk, or related metrics. 
 Experience using scripting or programming tools such as Python or MATLAB for data analysis, automation, or engineering debug. 
 Ability to work hands-on in a lab environment and interpret electrical, optical, manufacturing, or system-level test results. 
 Strong communication skills, with the ability to present technical findings, trade-offs, and recommendations to cross-functional engineering and program teams. 
 Assets:  
 Demonstrated interest in prototyping, embedded hardware, hardware bring-up, or lab-based debug projects. 
 Familiarity with coherent optical transceivers, optical modems, DSP-based systems, or high-speed communications hardware. 
 Familiarity with high-volume manufacturing, manufacturing test flows, factory yield analysis, or production data systems. 
 Experience with optical test equipment, electrical test equipment, automated test platforms, reliability qualification testing, failure analysis, or root-cause corrective action processes.

Maple’s purpose is to meet the world's healthcare needs. We’re Canada's leading on-demand healthcare platform, connecting patients with Canadian-licensed doctors, nurse practitioners and specialists. Today, we’re proud that over 8 million patients and 7,000 businesses and government partners have access to same-day, proactive and ongoing care. We enable people to take control of their health and push the boundaries of what’s possible every day.  

Bold minds. Big impact. A career at Maple is about making an impact. We empower bold thinking, surround you with an inspiring team and are driven by a motivating purpose. Here, you’ll do work that changes lives—including your own.

The role : As we grow, expand into new products, and prepare for scale, the engineers building Maple's products need a foundation that lets them move fast, safely, and autonomously. We're looking for a Director, Platform Engineering to build that foundation — and lead the team behind it. That’s where you come in. 
In this role, you'll stand up a new team whose customer is every other engineer at Maple. You'll own the developer experience end to end: CI/CD, deployment automation, observability, AI-assisted development tooling, test infrastructure, and the developer-facing infrastructure layer. This is a chance to define a platform mandate from scratch, partner directly with the VP of Engineering and CTO, and shape how Maple's engineering team builds software as we scale. The work you do here will compound — every hour your team saves a product engineer is an hour that goes back into the patient and provider experience.
Your responsibilities : As the Director of Platform Engineering, you’ll: 
 Own the platform engineering team's mandate end-to-end: developer environment, CI/CD and deployment pipelines, test infrastructure and quality tooling, framework and dependency health, AI tooling for engineers, and the AI feature tooling stack
 Serve Maple's product engineering squads as your primary customer — publish a platform roadmap, run developer surveys, and make prioritization calls based on developer friction data
 Drive engineering metrics in partnership with the VP of Engineering — stand up the tooling to measure developer experience, define the quantitative baselines, and set the roadmap to move them
 Hire, coach, and grow a small team of engineers, and set the operating model, rituals, and career expectations for the team
 Partner across Engineering, Business Technology, Security, Data, and Product to lead change — from shifting the org from manual to continuous deployment, to raising the bar on quality, observability, and incident response
 Stay hands-on where it matters: architecture reviews, prototyping, and unblocking your direct reports — while making sure the platform team stays a thin, high-leverage layer rather than an over-engineered one
 Translate platform investment into business outcomes for non-technical executive leaders and connect the team's roadmap to Maple's growth priorities
What success looks like : In your first 90 days, you'll have published a clear operating model and quarterly roadmap, and launched a baseline developer experience survey with a live metrics dashboard. You'll have built the hiring plan paired with roles and responsibilities for any open positions, and shipped a first handful of quick wins for the Product Engineering squads.
 In the following 12–18 months, you'll have moved Maple to continuous deployment on both backend and frontend, established a framework upgrade cadence that keeps the stack healthy, and matured E2E test infrastructure that runs on every PR. You'll have formalized incident management and an on-call rotation, matured our agentic engineering tooling, and put an AI evaluation harness in place. DORA metrics will trend into the "elite" range, developer experience survey scores will be measurably up, and the PR cycle time and code review burden will be measurably down — with the data to prove it.
What you bring: 5+ years of people leadership experience in engineering, including 2+ years building or leading a platform or developer experience team
 Director-level operating experience — you've owned a multi-domain technical roadmap and worked as a peer to other Directors and senior cross-functional leaders
 A track record of treating platform as a product — publishing roadmaps to internal customers, running developer surveys, setting up DevEx metrics, and making priority calls based on developer friction data, with a "thin platform" bias and a servant leadership orientation
 Deep expertise in modern CI/CD and deployment pipelines (GitHub Actions or equivalent, feature flag systems, progressive delivery, automated quality gates), and cloud infrastructure fluency (AWS preferred) — enough to be a credible counterpart to Business Technology in technical conversations
 Strong grounding in observability, incident management, and quality engineering — Datadog, SLOs, on-call design, blameless postmortems, E2E test frameworks, and shift-left quality
 Hands-on familiarity with AI-assisted development tooling (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, agent infrastructure) — you've actually shipped or operated AI tooling for engineers, not just watched the space
 A strong change management track record — you've led org-wide engineering transitions before (for example, shifting an org from manual to continuous deployment), and know how to build the case, sequence the rollout, and land the change without stalling delivery
 Strong written communication and comfort with ambiguity — you're joining a team that doesn't yet exist, and you know how to write decision docs, RFCs, and roadmaps that travel well in a hybrid org
 Play to your strengths. Finding the right fit goes both ways—so this section is yours to complete. When you join, you'll add the unique strengths you bring that aren't captured above.
Our tech stack: Here's the stack we're building with today. Curiosity and a strong learning mindset matter more to us than hands-on experience with every tool below:
 Backend: Built on Laravel PHP framework, with multiple integration services, such as Langfuse
 Frontend: React Native Web for a unified codebase across web and mobile, Typescript and styled components; we also leverage Alpine, Livewire and Tailwind
 Databases: Multi-database architecture with MySQL 8 and Amazon DocumentDB, Redis for caching, and Typesense for search engine indexing
 Infrastructure & DevOps: Containerized, auto-scaling architecture built on top of AWS; Infrastructure-as-Code setup with Terraform and GitHub Actions 
 Testing & QA: We utilize a number of testing tools for unit, integration, end-to-end and accessibility testing, such as PHPUnit, Jest, WebDriverIO, and axe-core
 Other tools & services: Monitoring and observability with Datadog, project management done through Jira, and BugSnag for error/crash monitoring
How we'll support you: We recognise our people's health is everything. That's why we take care of them.
 Maple for you and your family: 24/7 access to general practitioners, pediatrics and mental health therapy for you and your family. Care starts on day one
 Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental and life insurance because your peace of mind—and your loved ones—matter most
 Health spending account: Extra funds to cover the essentials that make a difference, from new glasses to specialised therapy

 Health days: Life happens. We provide 10 dedicated days for rest, medical appointments or caregiving, so you can show up at your best
 Destination days: Work from anywhere. Enjoy the flexibility to work internationally in eligible countries for up to five days per year
 Group retirement savings plan: We're here for the long haul. Invest in your future with our group retirement plan

Ce rôle s’adresse à une personne capable de relier les objectifs d’affaires des clients à la stratégie marketing, de challenger avec intention et de diriger un portefeuille de comptes ciblé en profondeur — plutôt que de disperser son attention sur une longue liste de clients gérés en surface.
 Ce poste n’est pas pour tout le monde. 
 Nous bâtissons quelque chose de rare : un endroit où la croissance, la vérité et la haute performance avancent ensemble.

 ✅ Vous avez dirigé des relations clients dans un environnement d’agence de marketing de performance.
✅ Vous comprenez comment les canaux marketing modernes fonctionnent ensemble — médias, SEO, création, données, CRM, site Web, CRO et analytique.
✅ Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads et de stratégie médias payants avec crédibilité.
✅ Les résultats d’affaires des clients vous importent plus que les simples indicateurs de campagne.
✅ Vous pouvez diriger un portefeuille ciblé de clients en profondeur, plutôt que gérer une énorme liste en surface.
✅ Votre réflexe naturel est « je m’en occupe », même lorsque le travail dépasse légèrement votre champ habituel.
 Et vous aurez de la difficulté ici si : 
 ❌ Votre expérience est principalement axée sur la marque, la création, le commerce électronique ou le DTC, sans expérience approfondie en agence de performance.
❌ Vous avez seulement géré des comptes en surface, dans un contexte de très grand volume de clients.

 À propos de Level
 Nous sommes une agence de marketing de performance propulsée par l’IA — bâtie pour la précision, conçue pour croître, et alimentée par une mentalité scientifique. Chez Level, nous combinons stratégie, médias, création et intelligence machine pour générer des résultats qui comptent. Chaque fois. À grande échelle.
 Nous avons été nommés parmi les meilleurs lieux de travail de Pittsburgh et reconnus comme l’une des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide du classement Inc. 500. Nos clients œuvrent notamment en B2B, en éducation, en santé, en services financiers, en commerce électronique et dans plusieurs autres secteurs.
 Votre rôle et votre impact
 À titre d’Account Director, vous dirigerez des relations clients axées sur la performance au sein d’un portefeuille de comptes ciblé. Vous serez au croisement de la stratégie client, de l’exécution marketing, du leadership auprès des équipes internes et de l’impact d’affaires.
 Vous serez la personne à qui les clients font confiance pour leur dire la vérité, celle sur qui les équipes internes comptent pour créer de la clarté, et celle qui garde la stratégie arrimée à des résultats mesurables.
 Vous devrez :
 Diriger la stratégie de performance : Traduire les objectifs d’affaires des clients en stratégies marketing multicanaux qui génèrent une croissance mesurable.
 Prendre en charge les relations clients : Bâtir la confiance avec les parties prenantes seniors grâce à une communication claire, une pensée proactive et des recommandations stratégiques solides.
 Relier l’écosystème marketing : Aider les clients à comprendre comment les médias payants, le SEO, la création, les données, le CRM, les sites Web, le CRO et le reporting travaillent ensemble pour améliorer la performance.
 Apporter une aisance en médias payants : Parler avec crédibilité de Google Ads, des médias sociaux payants et de la performance média — même si vous n’êtes pas la personne qui effectue chaque changement dans les plateformes.

 Gérer un portefeuille en profondeur : Diriger un portefeuille ciblé de comptes avec suffisamment de profondeur pour vraiment comprendre les activités, les leviers de performance et les risques de chaque client.
 Guider les équipes internes : Collaborer avec les équipes médias, SEO, création, analytique et stratégie afin de faire avancer le travail, clarifier les priorités et aligner les résultats.
 Raconter l’histoire dans les données : Transformer les rapports, les tableaux de bord et les analyses de performance en insights que les clients peuvent mettre en action.
 Maîtriser les détails : Garder les budgets, prévisions, échéanciers, documents et communications clairs, exacts et à jour.
 Exigences
 Essentiels
 5 ans et plus dans une agence de marketing de performance. Vous avez une expérience en agence ancrée dans la performance, les médias payants et les résultats mesurables — et non principalement dans la marque, la création ou le commerce électronique seulement.
 Expérience en leadership de comptes dans un environnement de performance. Vous êtes actuellement Account Director dans une agence de marketing de performance, ou vous avez commencé en marketing, médias payants, analytique ou gestion de campagnes avant de faire la transition vers le leadership de comptes.
 Aisance obligatoire avec Google Ads. Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads avec crédibilité et savez quoi examiner lorsque la performance fluctue, que le volume de leads baisse ou que la qualité des conversions change.
 Compréhension de l’écosystème marketing moderne. Vous comprenez comment les médias payants, le SEO, la création, les données, le CRM, les sites Web, le CRO et l’analytique se connectent pour générer des résultats.
 Solide profondeur en stratégie médias payants. Vous comprenez comment les canaux médias fonctionnent ensemble, particulièrement le search et le social, et pouvez traduire les signaux de performance en stratégie.

 Expérience avec des budgets médias significatifs. Vous avez travaillé avec des clients qui investissent au moins 50 000 $ par mois en médias par client; 100 000 $ et plus par mois est fortement souhaité.
 Mentalité orientée affaires. Vous parlez de revenus, de pipeline, de qualité des leads, de parcours de conversion, de parcours client et de résultats d’affaires — pas seulement de CTR, de CPC et de métriques de plateforme.
 Peu d’ego, beaucoup d’ownership. Vous êtes prêt ou prête à construire le tableau de bord, chercher la réponse, clarifier l’ambiguïté ou combler l’écart lorsque l’équipe en a besoin.
 Fortement souhaités
 Expérience en B2B, génération de leads ou ventes complexes. Une expérience avec des cycles d’achat plus longs, la qualité du pipeline, l’alignement avec les ventes ou des parcours de conversion non DTC est un grand atout.
 Aisance avec Meta, LinkedIn, le SEO, le CRM, le CRO ou d’autres canaux. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être expert ou experte dans chaque canal, mais vous devez comprendre comment ils fonctionnent ensemble.
 Expérience dans les services financiers, la santé, l’éducation, le SaaS ou d’autres secteurs à achat réfléchi.
 Aisance avec les tableaux de bord, les outils de reporting, Google Analytics et la visualisation de données.
 Expérience en mentorat auprès de membres d’équipes de comptes ou en coordination d’équipes de livraison interfonctionnelles.
 Attentes liées à l’IA
 Chez Level, l’IA est une compétence — pas un raccourci. Dans ce rôle, on s’attendra à ce que vous puissiez :
 Utiliser des outils comme ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude et Perplexity pour améliorer votre façon de travailler
 Partager vos prompts, vos améliorations de processus et vos idées avec l’équipe
 Expérimenter régulièrement et raffiner vos façons de travailler au fil du temps
 Accueillir l’inconfort comme une partie normale du processus d’apprentissage
 Appliquer les outils d’IA pour augmenter votre vitesse, votre clarté et votre créativité — sans remplacer un travail réfléchi
 L’IA devrait vous rendre plus aiguisé ou aiguisée, plus rapide et plus stratégique. Elle ne devrait jamais remplacer le jugement, le goût, l’imputabilité ou un point de vue solide.
 Nos valeurs fondamentales
 Pas d’ego, engagement total
 Chez nous, « ce n’est pas mon travail » n’a pas sa place. Nous gagnons ensemble, nous prêtons main-forte là où il le faut, et nous nous soucions davantage du résultat que de l’organigramme.
 Meilleur chaque jour

 Obsédés par les résultats

 Guidés par la vérité
 Nous remettons les hypothèses en question, suivons les données et disons aux clients ce qu’ils doivent entendre — pas seulement ce qui est facile à dire.
 Avantages et bénéfices

 Cotisations de retraite de l’employeur : 401(k) aux États-Unis et contribution REER au Canada

 Télétravail d’abord
 Ce poste est ouvert aux personnes résidant aux États-Unis et au Canada et est entièrement en télétravail. Nous ne sommes pas en mesure de commanditer des visas pour le moment.
 Level est fondée sur l’inclusion
 Nous sommes engagés envers la diversité, l’équité, l’inclusion et l’appartenance. Level est fière d’être un employeur souscrivant au principe de l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi — nous célébrons ce qui fait de vous une personne unique.

WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

As a Workplace Project Manager, you'll take our workplace playbooks and standards and turn them into delivered projects and programs on the ground - office moves and openings, and global special projects like health & safety programming, design standards, emergency response planning, WVPPs, sustainability, and new tooling rollouts. This is a hands-on delivery role: you own scope, schedule, and budget for each project or program and drive it from kickoff to close.



Where the program sets the standard, your projects and programs bring it to life - on time, on budget, and to spec.







WHAT YOU'LL DO



Global Special Projects



 - Project manage Workplace's global special projects: health & safety (H&S) programming, global design standards, global emergency response programming, Workplace Violence Prevention Plans (WVPPs), and sustainability programming across Harvey's office portfolio.

 - Partner with Security, HR, Legal, and regional Workplace leads to build and roll out emergency response plans and WVPPs that meet local regulatory requirements while staying consistent with Harvey's global standards.

 - Maintain and evolve global design standards (furniture, finishes, signage) so offices feel consistently "Harvey" as we scale into new markets.

 - Drive sustainability initiatives across offices - vendor and materials selection, energy and waste programs - and track progress against goals.

 - Own the global rollout of Workplace tooling and software - evaluating, piloting, and implementing platforms like desk booking, occupancy, and ticketing, and driving stakeholder training and adoption.

 - Own global and national vendor contracts (F&B, janitorial, plants, and similar categories) - procurement, negotiation, and the master vendor relationship - while regional workplace managers own the day-to-day relationship, performance, and feedback in their offices.




Global Playbook & Portfolio Management (Moves & Openings)

 - Build and maintain the FDOB checklist and playbook that regional workplace leads execute against for satellite moves, expansions, and new-office openings.

 - Own the portfolio-level calendar tracking when and where expansions and new offices are happening across the org, so Workplace can sequence and resource projects appropriately.

 - Step in to lead a move, opening, or buildout directly where a region doesn't yet have an established workplace manager, or where the existing regional team doesn't have the bandwidth - expect this to be a shrinking share of the role over time as regional coverage matures.

 - Coordinate with IT, Security, and AV to keep day-one readiness standards current in the playbook, so regional teams can deliver consistently without you running each project personally.



Program Management



 - Build and maintain project plans, schedules, and budgets across global programs and the FDOB playbook; track milestones, dependencies, and risks, and communicate status clearly to stakeholders and leadership.

 - Maintain the portfolio-level view across all in-flight and planned moves, openings, and buildouts, flagging sequencing and resourcing risks to leadership.

 - Manage vendor relationships tied to your global contracts and programs, holding them accountable to schedule and quality.

 - Report to the Global Workplace Operations Manager to ensure every program and playbook meets Harvey's workplace standards and sets regional teams up for smooth steady-state operations.







WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years in workplace operations, program management, or project management, with experience leading cross-functional programs such as health & safety, emergency preparedness, sustainability, or systems/tooling rollouts.

 - Strong program design and playbook-building instincts - you'd rather build a system and standard that others execute against well than run every project yourself.

 - Experience managing vendor and procurement relationships at a national or global scale.

 - Strong command of project management fundamentals - scope, schedule, budget, risk, and stakeholder communication.

 - Experience partnering with (not necessarily owning) construction, real estate, or facilities teams on office moves or buildouts.

 - Excellent organizational and communication skills; you keep complex, fast-moving programs on track and everyone informed.

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a hands-on, get-it-done approach.

 - Based in Toronto and able to work on-site at our Toronto office, with willingness to travel to other sites as projects require.




NICE TO HAVE 

 - Experience building or administering H&S programs, emergency response plans, or WVPPs.

 - Experience with sustainability program design or reporting.

 - Familiarity with project / workplace tools - e.g., Asana, Smartsheet, Envoy, OfficeSpace.

 - Experience building playbooks or programs that scale across a distributed, multi-region team.

Our culture

ELYSIS – Conseiller Sénior technologies réfractaires
 Une nouvelle ère pour l’industrie de l’aluminium – ELYSIS
 Aluminium sans carbone
 La technologie ELYSIS™ représente la plus grande avancée dans l’industrie de l’aluminium depuis 1886. Des efforts sont présentement déployés afin de perfectionner cette nouvelle façon révolutionnaire de produire de l’aluminium, qui élimine le dioxyde de carbone et toutes les autres émissions de gaz à effet de serre du procédé conventionnel d’électrolyse.
 Le procédé ELYSIS élimine l’utilisation d’anodes de carbone, en les remplaçant par des matériaux brevetés. En tant que premier procédé industriel qui émet de l’oxygène comme sous-produit, il a le potentiel de transformer toute l’industrie.
 En 2018, deux producteurs d’aluminium de calibre international, Alcoa et Rio Tinto, ont uni leurs forces afin de créer la coentreprise ELYSIS avec le gouvernement du Québec. Bénéficiant du soutien du gouvernement du Canada et la technologie progresse et elle est actuellement conçue pour être utilisée aussi bien dans des projets de construction que de modernisation d’alumineries. 
 ELYSIS a son siège social à Montréal, avec des centres de recherche et de développement à Alma et à Jonquière, au Québec (Canada), ainsi qu’à New Kensington, en Pennsylvanie (États-Unis) et en France.
 Du métal de qualité commerciale produit par ELYSIS dans nos installations R&D et au centre de développement industriel est déjà utilisé par Apple dans un éventail de produits (comme le MacBook Pro 16 po et l’iPhone SE), par AB InBev (canettes) et par Audi (roues du e-tron GT, fabriquées par le RONAL Group).
 Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’ELYSIS!
 À propos du poste
 Êtes-vous prêt(e) à relever un nouveau défi passionnant? À titre de Spécialiste en technologie des matériaux réfractaires, vous aurez l’occasion de démontrer votre esprit d’innovation en développant de nouvelles idées et de nouveaux concepts afin de les transformer en opportunités concrètes chez ELYSIS.
 Relevant du Leader Technologie Électrolyse, vous serez responsable de faire progresser le niveau de maturité de la technologie ELYSIS en ce qui concerne les composants réfractaires et multi-matériaux des assemblages d’électrodes ainsi que d’autres systèmes.
 Principales responsabilités
 Le ou la Spécialiste en technologie des matériaux réfractaires travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d’ELYSIS des secteurs Technologie, Industrialisation et Opérations afin de concrétiser de nouveaux concepts. Vous ferez partie d’une équipe qui dirige les activités de développement technologique tout en identifiant les possibilités futures d’amélioration des systèmes et technologies existants.
 • Maintenir une attention constante envers l’environnement, la santé et la sécurité (ESS).
 • Mettre à profit une expertise approfondie des matériaux réfractaires, de l’assemblage mécanique, de la conception et des principes d’ingénierie afin d’accélérer le développement et la commercialisation des assemblages d’électrodes ELYSIS et d’autres systèmes.
 • Développer, valider et mettre en œuvre de nouvelles méthodes d’essais en laboratoire et sur le terrain afin d’évaluer la performance, la durabilité et la pertinence des matériaux réfractaires pour des applications spécifiques.
 • Réaliser des évaluations de compatibilité des matériaux afin de déterminer les interactions entre les réfractaires, les matériaux de procédé, les atmosphères d’exploitation et les conditions de service à haute température.
 • Vérifier et qualifier la qualité des matières premières reçues au moyen de techniques de caractérisation physique, chimique, minéralogique et microstructurale.
 • Développer et mettre en œuvre un portefeuille de projets de R-D portant sur les composants des assemblages d’électrodes, définir des objectifs clairs et diriger les efforts d’innovation afin de faire progresser les solutions industrielles pour les assemblages d’électrodes ELYSIS et d’autres systèmes.
 • Faire progresser le niveau de maturité technologique (TRL) de la technologie ELYSIS en collaboration avec les équipes de modélisation avancée, de recherche fondamentale et d’opérations pilotes.
 • Élaborer et exécuter, en collaboration avec l’équipe d’industrialisation, un plan visant à optimiser la conception et la fabricabilité d’un assemblage multi-matériaux, dans l’optique de systèmes de fabrication automatisés à grand volume et à faible coût permettant d’atteindre les objectifs commerciaux et d’affaires.
 • Développer et mettre en œuvre un portefeuille de projets visant à démontrer la performance des assemblages d’électrodes en cellule, définir des objectifs clairs et des résultats économiques incluant les coûts d’exploitation et d’investissement, assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance clés (portée, échéancier et budget) et diriger les efforts d’innovation technologique.
 • Assurer l’exécution des projets conformément à la feuille de route établie, en collaboration avec les équipes d’industrialisation et des opérations (internes et/ou clients).
 • Assurer la coordination et l’alignement entre les objectifs de modélisation, de recherche fondamentale, d’expérimentations en laboratoire et en cellule, d’analyses post-mortem (autopsies) et autres, tout en favorisant la collaboration entre les différents départements.
 • Résoudre les problèmes à leur cause fondamentale, identifier les possibilités d’amélioration et mettre en œuvre les solutions requises pour améliorer les matériaux et les procédés.
 • Identifier et mettre en œuvre des initiatives de réduction des coûts visant à fournir des solutions techniques économiques pour les composants critiques des assemblages.
 • Favoriser des relations de collaboration avec les départements des opérations, de l’industrialisation et de la technologie afin d’assurer une efficacité optimale et d’accélérer le déploiement technologique.
 • Adapter et modifier les solutions technologiques en fonction des résultats obtenus afin d’atteindre les objectifs de la feuille de route.
 • Promouvoir une culture d’innovation et assurer l’exécution réussie de la feuille de route technologique d’ELYSIS ainsi que la réalisation d’avancées technologiques majeures.
 • Présenter les résultats, les apprentissages et les conclusions au moyen de rapports techniques, de présentations, de brevets et de publications afin de favoriser le transfert des connaissances et l’alignement stratégique.
 Profil recherché
 Pour réussir dans ce rôle et contribuer à notre succès continu, nous recherchons une personne possédant les qualifications suivantes :
 • Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en science et génie des matériaux, en génie mécanique, en génie industriel, en génie manufacturier ou dans un domaine scientifique connexe.
 • Minimum de 10 années d’expérience pratique ainsi qu’une connaissance approfondie de la corrosion des matériaux réfractaires et multi-matériaux ainsi que de l’assemblage industriel.
 • Une expérience en fabrication industrielle, en fabrication de produits ou dans les principes de conception de lignes d’assemblage constitue un atout.
 • Expérience de gestion d’équipes techniques comprenant des ingénieurs, des scientifiques ou des techniciens.
 • Excellente compréhension des matériaux réfractaires, notamment l’alumine, la silice, la magnésie et les réfractaires contenant du carbone.
 • Connaissance des mécanismes de dégradation à haute température tels que la corrosion, l’érosion, les chocs thermiques, l’oxydation et les attaques chimiques.
 • Compréhension de la compatibilité entre les matériaux réfractaires et les métaux en fusion, les scories, les gaz, les produits chimiques de procédé et les autres environnements d’exploitation.
 • Connaissance des normes ASTM, ISO et des standards de l’industrie applicables aux essais et à la qualification des matériaux réfractaires.
 • Maîtrise de SolidWorks ou AutoCAD ainsi que d’ANSYS ou d’outils similaires utilisés pour la simulation, la conception et les essais.
 • Excellentes compétences en gestion de projets et historique démontré de réalisation de projets dans les délais et selon la portée prévue.
 • Excellente aptitude à effectuer des présentations et à enseigner ou expliquer des contenus et concepts techniques.
 • Capacité à influencer sans détenir d’autorité hiérarchique directe.
 • Faire preuve de vision, savoir écouter, comprendre les défis et identifier des opportunités que d’autres ne perçoivent pas.
 • Comprendre les fondements de la science des matériaux.
 • Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles et en communication.

 • Excellent esprit d’équipe et grande capacité de collaboration.
 • Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit. Notre organisation est une entreprise mondiale et les fonctions de ce poste nécessitent une collaboration quotidienne avec des collègues, des équipes ou des partenaires basés à l'extérieur du Québec
 • Passion pour la résolution de défis techniques complexes afin de faire progresser une innovation de rupture visant à atténuer la crise climatique dans une industrie difficile à décarboner.

 Canada

 ELYSIS™ procure également des avantages additionnels, en réduisant les coûts d’exploitation des alumineries et en augmentant la production de métal par rapport aux cuves conventionnelles de même taille.

 Carbon Free Aluminium

 The ELYSIS™ technology eliminates all direct greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from the aluminium smelting process and is the first industrial process that emits oxygen as its by-product.
 ELYSIS has demonstrated production of commercial purity aluminium for end users ranging from Apple to Audi and is being designed for the construction of new smelters or to retrofit existing ones.
 The ELYSIS™ technology also brings additional advantages, reducing the operating cost of a smelter and boosting metal production from the same size-smelting cell.
 About the Location
 ELYSIS is a Canadian based firm with its corporate headquarters in Montréal, Quebec. Its other Canadian locations include Alma, Québec and Jonquière, Québec. It is at ELYSIS’ Alma, Québec location where eliminating all direct greenhouse gases from aluminium smelting took a major step forward in June 2021 with the start of construction on the first commercial-scale prototype cells of ELYSIS’ inert anode technology, at Rio Tinto’s Alma, Québec smelter. At ELYSIS’ Jonquière, Québec Location, ELYSIS is further developing this technology at its Research and Development Centre, located within Rio Tinto’s Complexe Jonquière.
 Be Part of an Unprecedented Partnership
 At ELYSIS we are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome — they are essential to success of the unprecedented partnership that ELYSIS is. We treat each other respectfully, fairly, compassionately and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different. At ELYSIS, we welcome and encourage applications from Indigenous people, women, members of the LGBTQ2S+ community, older workers, people with disabilities and representatives of diverse backgrounds.
 About Rio Tinto 
 Rio Tinto is a leading global mining and materials company. We operate in 35 countries where we produce iron ore, copper, aluminium, critical minerals, and other materials needed for the global energy transition and for people, communities, and nations to thrive.
 We have been mining for 150 years and operate with knowledge built up across generations and continents. Our purpose is finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs – striving for innovation and continuous improvement to produce materials with low emissions and to the right environmental, social and governance standards. But we can’t do it on our own, so we’re focused on creating partnerships to solve problems, create win-win situations and meet opportunities.
 Respect and Inclusion

 We are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel comfortable to be themselves. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard, all cultures respected and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome – they are essential to our success. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different.
 À propos de Rio Tinto 
 Rio Tinto est un chef de file mondial du secteur des sociétés minières et des matériaux. Nous sommes établis dans 35 pays où nous produisons du minerai de fer, du cuivre, de l’aluminium, des minéraux critiques et d’autres matériaux nécessaires à la transition énergétique mondiale et à la prospérité des personnes, des communautés et des nations. 
 Nous exerçons nos activités depuis 150 ans, en nous appuyant sur les connaissances accumulées au fil des générations et sur les différents continents. Notre mission – trouver de meilleures façons de fournir les matériaux dont le monde a besoin – nous guide dans notre quête d’innovation et d’amélioration continue, dans le but de fabriquer des produits à faibles émissions et répondant aux bonnes normes environnementales, sociales et de gouvernance. Mais comme nous ne pouvons pas y arriver seuls, nous nous attachons à créer des partenariats nous permettant de résoudre des problèmes, de créer des situations mutuellement avantageuses et de saisir des occasions.
 Respect and Inclusion 
Chez Rio Tinto, nous accueillons favorablement et encourageons les candidatures d’Autochtones, de femmes, de membres de la communauté LGBTQ+, de travailleurs âgés, de personnes handicapées et de représentants d’origines diverses.

Nous nous traitons mutuellement avec équité et dignité, sans égard à la race, au genre, à la nationalité, à l’origine ethnique, à la religion, à l’âge, à l’orientation sexuelle ou à tout autre aspect distinctif.

The position manages installation and maintenance of software programs and laboratory equipment, monitors and maintains consumable supply inventories, provides logistical and instructional support of laboratory-based courses, instructs undergraduate students in specific technological, laboratory and research skills, and provides logistical support of faculty research programs.

Our department is committed to contributing to an educational environment that is rich with a wide range of intellectual perspectives and backgrounds.

 Assists faculty with technical instruction of lectures and laboratories, including presenting laboratory demonstrations and common research-related content such as research ethics, IRB and IACUC protocols, policies and guidelines.
 Assists in preparing chemical solutions, sets up instrumentation, and ensures adequate supplies for classroom demonstrations, course laboratories, and faculty research projects.
 Assists in the teaching mission of the department by supporting faculty in the development of new experiments, demonstrations, and activities for teaching labs and courses.
 Assists students with course projects, independent studies, research design, statistical procedures, and written feedback on IRB proposals to facilitate IRB approval and project development.
 Coordinates with animal care staff and assists in training and oversight of students in support of faculty teaching and research programs to ensure compliance with IACUC standards and IACUC-approved animal use protocols. Assists faculty in training and oversight of students in animal behavioral and histological procedures. 
 Develops, maintains, and disseminates procedures for equitable in-person participant recruitment for course-related and programmatic research.
 Supports productive and efficient faculty research programs by assisting faculty with logistics of conducting research.

 Performs other related duties as assigned.

 Bachelor’s degree in psychology, neuroscience, or allied discipline. Formal postgraduate training or degree preferred.
 Experience working in a behavioral science laboratory (psychology or behavioral neuroscience setting preferred).

 Ability to assist with the care, handling, and use of laboratory animals, or willingness to acquire these skills.
 Knowledge of laboratory safety, chemical storage, hazardous materials handling, and Safety Data Sheets, or willingness to acquire this knowledge.
 Ability to work independently, as well as to communicate and interact effectively in a professional and courteous manner with faculty, staff and students.

 About this position:
 We're looking for a Senior Security Engineer to strengthen Later's company-wide security posture through hands-on engineering, thoughtful collaboration, and pragmatic standards. This role blends deep security expertise with strong software engineering skills, with a focus on application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development practices, vulnerability management, compliance enablement, and security improvements across our corporate systems and business operations. You'll partner closely with teams across Engineering, Infrastructure, Product, IT, Legal, People, Finance, and other business functions to embed security into Later's systems, tools, workflows, and operating practices. A core focus of this role is helping Later mature its security capabilities in support of SOC 2 and other compliance expectations through practical controls, automation, evidence-ready processes, and clear guidance that works across the company. This role is ideal for a senior security practitioner who thinks like a defender, builds like a software engineer, and leads through influence across both technical and non-technical teams.
 What you'll be doing:
 Company-Wide Security Strategy & Compliance 
 Assess and continuously improve Later's overall security posture across applications, infrastructure, cloud environments, corporate systems, vendor tooling, and business workflows.
 Define and implement scalable security standards, best practices, and guardrails that support SOC 2 readiness through practical, automated, and auditable solutions.
 Partner with Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, Product, Legal, People, Finance, and business leaders to align security priorities with company goals, risk reduction, and delivery timelines.
 Translate SOC 2 and related compliance requirements into sustainable technical and operational controls, procedures, and evidence collection practices.
 Identify security gaps across the company, prioritize remediation efforts, and help teams make pragmatic, risk-based decisions.
 Support company-wide security awareness, secure operating practices, and adoption of security controls across business teams.
 Technical Execution 
 Build and maintain internal security tools, automation, and services that support secure development, compliance workflows, vulnerability management, corporate security operations, and operational visibility.
 Design and implement security controls within CI/CD pipelines, including secure build and deploy patterns, security scanning, dependency management, container scanning, and secret management.
 Support application security efforts, including secure design reviews, threat modeling, code review guidance, API security, microservices security patterns, and remediation planning.
 Improve cloud infrastructure and corporate systems security through hardening, monitoring, configuration review, Infrastructure-as-Code security scanning, access reviews, and secure operational patterns.
 Collaborate with technical and business teams to identify vulnerabilities and control gaps, explain impact clearly, and drive effective remediation.
 Strengthen security observability and response readiness through logging, alerting, detection engineering, incident response improvements, and company-wide security process maturity.
 Collaboration & Enablement 
 Partner with teams across the company to identify, understand, and fix security issues in a collaborative, non-blocking way.
 Provide pragmatic security guidance on designs, implementations, vendor tools, operational practices, and business workflows.
 Communicate security risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations clearly across technical and non-technical audiences.
 Embed security into development workflows, corporate systems, and company operating practices without slowing teams unnecessarily.
 Support SOC 2 and related compliance efforts through automation, well-defined controls, reliable evidence practices, and cross-functional coordination.
 What success looks like:
 Within the first 90 days, you've completed a security posture assessment, identified the highest-priority gaps, and have a remediation roadmap that's been reviewed and socialized with key stakeholders across Engineering, IT, and Leadership.
 By 6 months, core SOC 2 controls are documented, automated where possible, and evidence collection is running reliably without manual heroics from any single team.
 Security is embedded into Later's CI/CD pipelines, with scanning, secret management, and container security integrated and maintained as a standard part of the development lifecycle.
 Teams across Engineering, IT, and the business have a clear point of contact for security questions, a shared understanding of the risk landscape, and security guidance that helps them move faster, not slower.
 Later's security observability has materially improved: logging, alerting, and detection coverage are in place, and the company has a documented, practiced incident response process.

 5-7+ years of experience as a Security Engineer or Software Engineer with a strong security focus.
 Proven ability to build and operate production-quality software, automation, and internal tooling.
 Strong understanding of application security, infrastructure security, cloud security, secure CI/CD practices, and corporate security controls.
 Hands-on experience with vulnerability management, secure software development, threat modeling, remediation workflows, and operational security improvements.
 Experience with security frameworks and standards such as OWASP, NIST, CIS Controls, SOC 2, and ISO 27001, and the ability to apply them in production and business environments.
 Experience supporting SOC 2 compliance efforts through practical, automated, and auditable controls.
 Familiarity with cloud security platforms such as AWS Security Hub, Azure Security Center, or GCP Security Command Center.
 Experience with SIEM/SOAR tools, logging and monitoring platforms, detection workflows, and practical incident response processes.
 Experience with Infrastructure-as-Code security scanning for tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
 Ability to translate complex security concepts into clear, actionable guidance for technical and non-technical audiences.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

À PROPOS DE LAMOUR 
 Entreprise familiale fondée en 1953, Lamour Inc. s’est forgé une solide réputation comme référence en matière de bas, vêtements de performance, bonneterie et lingerie. Nous faisons partie des 5 plus grands acteurs mondiaux dans les essentiels d’activewear, sommes le leader mondial du vêtement sans couture, et l’un des principaux fabricants de bas au Canada.
 En tant que guichet unique, nous travaillons avec innovation et passion afin d’offrir une qualité exceptionnelle et une grande valeur ajoutée à une clientèle internationale diversifiée. Notre succès repose sur notre expertise en technologies de tissus de performance, notre capacité d’innovation produit, nos investissements en excellence manufacturière, notre rapidité d’exécution, ainsi que la performance de notre chaîne d’approvisionnement, nous permettant de bâtir des partenariats solides, durables et significatifs à travers plusieurs réseaux de distribution.
 CE QUE NOUS RECHERCHONS 
 Relevant du directrice des finances, le ou la comptable principal(e) jouera un rôle clé dans l’exactitude et l’intégrité de l’information financière de Lamour. Il s’agit d’un poste opérationnel (« hands-on ») destiné à un(e) professionnel(le) de la comptabilité rigoureux(se), qui évolue aisément dans un environnement dynamique et qui possède de solides compétences analytiques pour gérer des fonctions complexes liées aux stocks, aux marges et à la comptabilité des coûts.
 RESPONSABILITÉS
 Préparer et examiner les états financiers mensuels, trimestriels et annuels conformément aux NCECF (ASPE) et aux politiques de l’entreprise 
 Être responsable des processus de clôture mensuelle, trimestrielle et annuelle, incluant les écritures de journal, les provisions et les rapprochements (allocations, redevances, paie, taxes de vente, etc.) 
 Prendre en charge les processus liés aux stocks et à la comptabilité des coûts, incluant l’évaluation des stocks, les provisions, les coûts d’acquisition (landed costs), la capitalisation du fret, le financement des fournisseurs, les impacts de change et l’analyse de la marge brute 
 Soutenir les consolidations mensuelles et la comptabilité intersociétés pour plusieurs entités juridiques, incluant les rapprochements et les éliminations 
 Participer aux initiatives d’optimisation de l’ERP et veiller à ce que les processus comptables, les contrôles et les rapports soient efficacement intégrés dans Business Central. Préparer et analyser les rapports de revenus et de marges, y compris l’analyse des écarts afin d’identifier les anomalies et les opportunités d’amélioration financière 
 Analyser les données et tendances financières afin de fournir des recommandations concrètes à la direction, y compris un soutien aux initiatives de budgétisation, de prévision et de planification stratégique 
 Contribuer à la préparation des rapports de gestion internes et des dossiers financiers destinés à la haute direction 
 Collaborer de manière transversale avec les équipes Finance opérationnelle, FP&A, Opérations, Marchandisage et Chaîne d’approvisionnement afin de fournir des analyses financières, répondre aux demandes et assurer une information financière précise et cohérente 
 Maintenir et soutenir les contrôles internes afin de protéger les actifs de l’entreprise et assurer la conformité aux exigences réglementaires 
 Coordonner et soutenir les audits externes, y compris la préparation des dossiers d’audit, des rapprochements et des réponses aux demandes des auditeurs 
 Identifier et mettre en œuvre des améliorations de processus et des initiatives d’automatisation afin d’accroître l’efficacité et les contrôles au sein de la fonction comptable 
 Participer à des projets spéciaux et à des analyses ponctuelles afin de soutenir les objectifs de l’entreprise; les responsabilités peuvent évoluer en fonction des besoins organisationnels 
 Fournir du mentorat et de l’encadrement aux membres plus juniors de l’équipe comptable, en soutenant leur développement technique et en révisant leur travail au besoin
 EXIGENCES ET COMPÉTENCES
 Titre de CPA requis ou en voie d’obtention, avec 5 à 8 ans d’expérience progressive en comptabilité, incluant une expérience pratique en préparation et analyse des états financiers; une expérience en audit est fortement souhaitée

 Solide expérience en comptabilité des stocks, coût des ventes et analyse des marges; une expérience dans les secteurs du commerce de détail, de gros ou des biens de consommation constitue un atout important 
 Expérience en audit externe 
 Bonne compréhension des principes, normes et réglementations comptables (NCECF / ASPE) 
 Maîtrise avancée de Microsoft Excel, incluant les tableaux croisés dynamiques, RECHERCHEV (VLOOKUP) et les formules complexes; une expérience avec Business Central ou un ERP similaire est un atout 
 Excellentes capacités analytiques et de résolution de problèmes, avec un grand souci du détail et un engagement envers l’amélioration continue 
 Excellentes compétences en communication, tant à l’oral qu’à l’écrit, avec la capacité de vulgariser des concepts financiers auprès de parties prenantes non financières 
 Capacité démontrée à travailler de manière autonome et en collaboration, en gérant plusieurs priorités et échéances avec un haut niveau d’intégrité et de professionnalisme 
 Le bilinguisme (français et anglais) est considéré comme un atout dans un environnement de siège social situé à Montréal

 ABOUT LAMOUR 
 Family-owned since 1953, Lamour Inc. has earned a reputation for being the best choice in socks, performance apparel, hosiery and lingerie. In fact, we're among the world's top 5 players in activewear basics, the world's leading manufacturer of seamless garments, and one of Canada's leading sock manufacturers. 
 As a one-stop shop, we work innovatively and passionately to deliver exceptional quality and value to a diverse international customer base. It's our focus on performance fabric technology and product innovation, investment in manufacturing excellence, speed-to-market and supply chain execution that enables us to build meaningful, strong and sustainable retail partnerships across multiple trade channels.
 WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 
 Reporting to the Director of Finance, the Senior Accountant will play a key role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of Lamour's financial reporting. This is a hands-on role for a detail-oriented accounting professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong analytical capabilities to complex inventory, margin, and cost accounting functions. 
 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Prepare and review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with ASPE and company policies 
 Own month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes, including journal entries, accruals, and reconciliations (Allowances, Royalties, Payroll, Sales Tax, and more) 
 Own inventory and cost accounting processes, including inventory valuation, reserves, landed costs, freight capitalization, vendor funding, foreign exchange impacts, and gross margin analysis. 
 Support monthly consolidations and intercompany accounting across multiple legal entities, including reconciliations and eliminations.  
 Support ongoing ERP optimization initiatives and ensure accounting processes, controls, and reporting are effectively integrated within Business Central. Prepare and analyze revenue and margin reporting, including variance analysis to identify discrepancies and opportunities for financial improvement 
 Analyze financial data and trends to provide actionable insights and recommendations to management, including support for budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning initiatives 
 Support the preparation of internal management reports and financial packages for senior leadership 
 Partner cross-functionally with Finance Ops, FP&A, Operations, Merchandising, and Supply Chain teams to provide financial analysis, respond to inquiries, and support accurate and consistent reporting 
 Maintain and support internal controls to safeguard company assets and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements 
 Coordinate and support external audits, including preparation of audit schedules, reconciliations, and responses to auditor inquiries 
 Identify and implement process improvements and automation initiatives to enhance efficiency and controls within the accounting function 
 Participate in special projects and ad hoc analyses to support business objectives; duties and responsibilities subject to change to meet business needs 
 Provide guidance and mentorship to junior accounting team members, supporting technical development and review of work where appropriate. 
 REQUIREMENTS 
 CPA designation required or actively in progress, with 5-8 years of progressive accounting experience including hands-on financial reporting and analysis; audit experience strongly preferred 
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field 
 Solid background in inventory accounting, cost of sales, and margin analysis, experience in retail, wholesale, or consumer goods is a strong asset 
 Experience with external audit 
 Strong understanding of accounting principles, standards, and regulations (ASPE) 
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, and complex formulas; experience with Business Central or similar ERP systems preferred 
 Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities with a keen attention to detail and a commitment to continuous improvement 
 Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to articulate financial concepts to non-financial stakeholders 
 Demonstrated ability to work independently and collaboratively, managing multiple priorities and deadlines with a high level of integrity and professionalism 
 Bilingualism (French and English) is considered an asset given our Montréal HQ environment 
 BENEFITS 
 Health & Dental – Insurance? We got you covered!
 Telemedicine – Access a doctor anytime, right from your phone!
 VRSP (Volunteer Retirement Savings Plan) – We help you save for the future!
 100% free public transit – Your commute is on us!
 Flex hours – Enjoy 12 flex days per year to work from home
 Free breakfast on Fridays – Start your last workday of the week with something tasty on us!
 Early Fridays – Wrap up at 1:30 PM in the summer!
 A gift card on your birthday – happy birthday from us to you!
 Summer rooftop terrace vibes – Work breaks with a view.
 5 à 7 summer hangout – Chill out at Esplanade Louvain, an outdoor space with gardens and music right next door.
 Team events & celebrations every month – Big thanks to our social committee for keeping the fun going!
